text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice where developers regularly merge their code into a shared repository. Each time new code is added, automated builds run to check that everything still works correctly. As part of this process, the team also runs tests automatically to make sure the new changes do not break existing features. The main benefit of CI is catching issues early, before they become big problems. This is possible thanks to CI pipelines, which are sets of automated steps that build, test, and verify the code. By using CI, teams can deliver software faster and with more confidence.
